questions.question: What makes an energy resource renewable on human timescales?
choices: It can never have environmental effects
It is replenished naturally fast enough for continued use under suitable conditions
It produces electricity without equipment
It exists in unlimited amounts everywhere

questions.question: Which energy resource's immediate availability is most directly reduced by thick daytime cloud cover?
choices: Geothermal energy
Stored coal
Solar energy
Uranium fuel

questions.question: What is geothermal energy?
choices: Energy from daily tides alone
Energy from sunlight reflected by clouds
Energy from burning atmospheric nitrogen
Energy from Earth's internal heat

questions.question: Which resource depends most directly on moving air?
choices: Wind energy
Nuclear fuel
Coal
Petroleum

questions.question: What is biomass as an energy resource?
choices: Any rock containing metal
Organic material that can provide energy
Only flowing seawater
Only solar panels

questions.question: What is an intermittent energy source?
choices: A source that never supplies energy
A source that must be radioactive
A source whose availability varies over time
A source that has no physical equipment

questions.question: Which resource supplies fuel for conventional nuclear fission power?
choices: Wind
Sunlight
Flowing water
Uranium

questions.question: Why are fossil fuels considered nonrenewable?
choices: They form far more slowly than they are commonly used
They are fully replaced during each annual growing season
They are replenished as quickly as electricity is used
They are called nonrenewable only because they produce heat

questions.question: Why can electricity storage help with wind and solar generation?
choices: It guarantees unlimited output from a generator
It can shift delivery from times of production to times of demand
It raises conversion efficiency to exactly 100%
It prevents every difference between generation and demand

questions.question: Why is renewable not the same as impact-free?
choices: Renewability guarantees no land or material requirements
Only fuel combustion can affect ecosystems
Equipment, land use, and material extraction can have effects
Manufacturing renewable equipment has no resource inputs

questions.question: What is a potential ecological tradeoff of a large hydroelectric dam?
choices: It always improves migration for every fish species
It leaves river sediment transport unchanged
It cannot affect habitats upstream
It can alter river flow and aquatic habitats

questions.question: Why can biomass be depleted despite being called renewable?
choices: Use can exceed regrowth or replenishment
Biomass cannot be replenished through plant growth
Burning biomass always causes regrowth at the same rate
Calling a source renewable guarantees sustainable use

questions.question: How can energy conservation reduce resource demand?
choices: It increases the amount of fuel needed for identical unnecessary use
Using less energy for unnecessary activities lowers required supply
It makes all generating resources unlimited
It only changes electricity prices, never consumption

questions.question: Why are local conditions important when choosing renewable energy projects?
choices: Every location has the same renewable potential
A project's size is the only factor that affects suitability
Sunlight, wind, water, geology, and ecological constraints vary
Ecological constraints matter only for fossil fuels

questions.question: How does energy efficiency differ from simply reducing a service?
choices: Efficiency means stopping every activity
Efficiency creates energy from nothing
Efficiency describes only fuel price
Efficiency provides a similar service with less energy

questions.question: A region has steady winds but few usable rivers. Which resource is most directly supported by these conditions?
choices: Wind generation
Large river hydropower
Coal formation each season
New uranium created by the wind

questions.question: A forest supplies 200 units of biomass yearly while 300 units are harvested. What happens if these rates persist?
choices: The stock necessarily grows
The biomass stock declines
Harvesting creates the missing biomass
The rates cannot affect the stock

questions.question: A solar system produces more electricity at midday than users need. Which measure can help meet evening demand?
choices: Operate the panels unchanged without light
Discard output that is not used immediately
Store some midday energy for later use
Assume evening demand will always be zero

questions.question: Two energy projects have equal electrical output. Which comparison better assesses environmental tradeoffs?
choices: Compare only their electrical output
Assume renewable projects have no impacts
Compare equipment color without examining the site
Compare land use, emissions, materials, and ecosystem effects
